title: Mastering Korean Particles: 은/는 vs 이/가
content: When learning Korean, one of the first major hurdles is understanding when to use 은/는 versus 이/가. The particle '은/는' is a topic marker. It is used to introduce a general topic or to contrast something. For example, '저는 학생입니다' (As for me, I am a student). On the other hand, '이/가' is a subject marker. It is used to point out a specific subject or highlight new information, especially when answering a question like 'Who is here?'. Understanding this subtle nuance will make your Korean sound much more natural!

title: Quick Guide to Korean Batchim (Final Consonants)
content: Batchim (받침) refers to the consonant located at the very bottom of a Korean syllable block. In English, it is often called the final consonant. When a consonant comes at the end of a syllable, it is usually not released fully like an initial consonant. For instance, the letters ㄱ, ㄲ, ㅋ all sound like a stopped 'k' sound at the end of a word. Mastering batchim rules is the secret to moving from a beginner accent to smooth, native-sounding pronunciation.
